pricing_detail: Sno Station is open source (Apache-2.0) with a free weekly cloud allowance; Plus $19/mo, Max $199/mo, pay-as-you-go balance from $10

name: Agent Tincan
description: Agent Tincan lets your AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, ChatGPT and others) ask each other to do things and hand back results through a small relay on your own Tailscale network, with no open ports or API keys between agents.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); runs on your own Tailscale network

name: Halofy
description: Halofy is an access and governance layer for a team's AI agents, giving every agent organizational context through one identity and policy model with provenance and audit, alongside a desktop AI workstation that turns power users' agent practices into shared policies.
pricing_detail: Free $0 (1 seat); Base $16/mo and Team $120/mo for 5 seats (billed yearly); Enterprise custom; governance layer AGPL-3.0

name: Robylon
description: Robylon builds AI customer-support agents that resolve tickets across email, chat, voice and WhatsApp, connect to helpdesks like Zendesk, Freshdesk and Intercom, take actions such as refunds and order updates, and hand hard cases to a person.
pricing_detail: Free Starter plan (300 credits/month); Pro from $25/mo; Business from $180/mo

name: Monobot.AI
description: Monobot.AI is a no-code platform for building voice and chat AI agents that handle customer support, bookings, reservations and routine business calls, with a workspace for managing agents and integrations with CRMs and other tools.
pricing_detail: Starter $200/mo, Growth $500/mo, Business $1,000/mo; Enterprise custom

name: Agent Barn
description: Agent Barn is an open-source (Apache-2.0) control plane for running a fleet of AI agents on your own Kubernetes: create, configure, run and monitor agents across Slack, Microsoft Teams and Telegram from one place.
pricing_detail: Self-hosted free (Apache-2.0); Cloud free for a limited time; supervised pilot $1,000

name: What Should My Bot Do
description: What Should My Bot Do is a free AI agent planner for small businesses: answer 5 quick questions and get a first agent to set up, 3 next jobs to automate and copy-ready templates for Grok Bot, ChatGPT, Claude and n8n. No signup.
pricing_detail: Planner and templates free, no signup; optional paid routines pack

name: SEAL
description: SEAL is an MCP server (npx sealnet-mcp) that lets AI agents send and request files and secrets with end-to-end encryption. After pairing, the default delivery route sends the file to the user's SEAL inbox and returns a handle to the model. Also has a browser app, CLI and SDK; free up to 1 GB per seal.
pricing_detail: Free up to 1 GB per seal; larger transfers after a one-time payment

name: ByteFlow
description: ByteFlow is a no-code builder for AI agents on top of the systems a company already runs (ERP, CRM, in-house and legacy apps) through APIs or a browser agent. Agents prepare the work, such as a CRM update or ERP entry, and a person approves it with one tap. Includes voice agents in 10+ Indian languages and document extraction.
pricing_detail: Paid; book a call for pricing

name: objekts Production Desk
description: objekts Production Desk is a free remote MCP server for planning AI/VFX, CGI, motion-design and animation production. Agents can check locked references, product, character and camera continuity, versioning risks and a sensible first proof of concept. Rough estimates only on request, and nothing is sent to the studio without the user's confirmation.
pricing_detail: Free remote MCP; production estimates on request

name: VirtualBudz BudBot
description: VirtualBudz BudBot is an AI budtender for cannabis dispensary websites. It answers shoppers' product questions, recommends items from the live menu and builds carts around the clock, so customers get help even when staff are busy.
pricing_detail: $100 per store per month; free trial

name: Loppee
description: Loppee is a US directory of local businesses that marks which ones it has verified (registration, an owner contact route and any required license). Its free, no-sign-in remote MCP server (loppee.com/mcp/discovery) and REST API let Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other assistants look up a business, read its Trust Card and identity-verified reviews, and compare options; owners can also manage their listing through their own AI agent.
pricing_detail: Free public MCP and REST reads with no sign-in; free for businesses to list, paid plans add reach and gallery space

name: remotify-mcp
description: remotify-mcp is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) local stdio MCP server (npx remotify-mcp) that gives Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and other MCP hosts a remote_exec tool for running shell commands on a remote computer through an HTTP relay. The remote machine needs only curl and bash (no SSH port or installed agent), and each command can wait for human approval or run automatically.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); the public relay at relay.remotify.run is free, or self-host it with Docker

name: HOL Guard
description: HOL Guard is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0), local-first security layer for AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot CLI. On supported integrations it checks risky shell commands, reads of secret-bearing files, package installs and new or changed MCP tools before they run, lets you allow, ask or block each action, and keeps a local record for review. It installs with pipx (hol-guard) and works offline; optional Guard Cloud adds synced approvals, team policy and dashboards.
pricing_detail: Free forever for local protection on one machine; Guard Cloud plans: Solo $4.99/mo, Pro $15/mo, Team $30/seat/mo, plus Enterprise

name: Bottally
description: Bottally is an AI marketing agent for SEO and AEO that runs on autopilot. Once you connect your blog (WordPress, Webflow, Ghost, Shopify, Wix, Notion, Framer, Next.js or a webhook), it researches keywords and competitor gaps, then writes and publishes one researched article a day with images. It also offers an opt-in backlink exchange network and tracks weekly whether ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Google AI Overviews and Perplexity recommend your business.
pricing_detail: One plan, $99/mo: 30 articles a month, weekly AI visibility tracking, keyword research and backlinks

name: Agentic Scientist
description: Sakana AI's open-source pipeline that turns coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI into AI scientists: from a task file they propose ideas, run and score experiments and ablations, then write the paper.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for the agent and model API keys or subscriptions you use

name: OpenGCUA
description: Open stack from Tongyi Lab's MAI-UI team for generalist computer-use agents that combine GUI clicks, accessibility trees, terminal commands, APIs and code: an OSWorld harness, a macOS real-device harness, a cross-device SDK and published task runs of eight frontier models.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); research preview

name: rtk
description: A CLI proxy that sits between coding agents and your shell and trims noisy command output before it reaches the model, cutting token use on everyday commands like tests, builds and git. Free and open source, with an RTK Pro tier for teams.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); RTK Pro adds team features.

name: Understand-Anything
description: Turns any codebase, knowledge base or docs folder into an interactive knowledge graph you can explore and question, working inside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and Gemini CLI.

name: Onlook
description: An open-source visual editor for React and Tailwind apps where you design on a canvas and an AI agent writes the code. Edit layouts like in Figma, then export clean code to your own repo.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); hosted cloud version in early access.

name: opcode
description: A desktop app for Claude Code that lets you manage sessions, build custom agents, track usage and browse project history from a GUI instead of the terminal.
pricing_detail: Open-source (AGPL-3.0); see site for any hosted plans

name: Memori
description: An LLM-, database- and framework-agnostic memory layer that turns what agents do and say into structured, persistent state they can recall in later runs. Open source to self-host, or use Memori Cloud with an API key.
pricing_detail: Open source to self-host; Memori Cloud has a free tier.

name: CloudCLI
description: A web and mobile interface for Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, so you can run and steer coding sessions from a browser or phone. Self-host free or use the hosted CloudCLI service.
pricing_detail: Free to self-host (AGPL); hosted CloudCLI from €7/month.

name: xerj
description: A local-first search engine and MCP server for agents: one Rust binary indexes code, docs, logs, CSV/JSONL and PDFs for full-text, vector and hybrid search plus agent memory, behind an Elasticsearch-compatible API.
pricing_detail: Free Community edition (Apache-2.0); paid Professional and Enterprise support.

name: Emdash
description: A free, open-source agentic development environment (YC W26) for running Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents in parallel, each in its own worktree, then reviewing diffs, PRs and CI in one place.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (Apache-2.0).

name: eve
description: Vercel's open-source agent framework, pitched as Next.js for agents: a file-system-based way to define an agent's tools, prompts and workflows and run it in production.

name: agentOS
description: A lightweight operating system for agents from Rivet that runs coding agents and their tools inside fast WebAssembly sandboxes with a file system, processes and networking, so you can spin up thousands cheaply.
pricing_detail: Free and open source; managed hosting through Rivet Cloud.

name: Agent Sandbox (Kubernetes)
description: A Kubernetes project that adds a Sandbox resource for running isolated, stateful agent workloads such as code execution and browsers, with warm pools and fast startup on your own cluster.

name: Toad
description: A terminal front end from Will McGugan (creator of Rich and Textual) for running AI coding agents like Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Codex through one polished, fast interface.

name: CodeCompanion.nvim
description: An AI coding plugin for Neovim with chat, inline edits and agent tools that can read files, run commands and edit code, working with Anthropic, OpenAI, Copilot, Ollama and other providers.

name: BaoCut
description: An AI video agent for macOS and Windows that transcribes, subtitles, translates, dubs, cuts and animates your footage from plain instructions, with every result landing in an editable timeline instead of a one-shot export.
pricing_detail: Free source-available desktop app (BaoCut Community License); separate license needed to resell BaoCut itself.

name: Libretto
description: An open-source CLI, debugging agents and browser tools for building and maintaining reliable web integrations, helping coding agents inspect real pages and write automations that keep working.

name: Phase
description: An open-source secrets manager that syncs API keys and environment variables to apps, CI and agents with end-to-end encryption and access control. Free tier, Pro from $10 per user a month, or self-host.
pricing_detail: Free plan; Pro $10 per user/month; self-host free.

name: Handsy
description: Lets an AI model use a real iPhone through a $7 ESP32 board that acts as a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, tapping and typing through apps with no jailbreak and no computer attached.

name: Doop
description: An open-source multiplayer design canvas with a design MCP server, so you and agents like Claude Code and Codex can design side by side on the same live canvas. Self-host or use Doop Cloud, free during beta.
pricing_detail: Open source (AGPL); Doop Cloud free during beta.

name: pooled
description: Peer-to-peer LLM inference in the browser: pool your laptops, phones and other devices into a room to run large open models for chat and coding agents, with no GPU server.

name: explainroo
description: Lets your AI coding agent make narrated explainer videos: it writes the script, builds the visuals and renders the voice and video on your own computer, with no API key needed. Free and open source.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); runs locally with no API key.

name: ThinkWatch Lite
description: A local gateway that sits between your coding agents and model providers, letting you switch upstreams, redact secrets before they leave your machine, block dangerous tool calls and see the cost of each request.

name: Eleven
description: An agent-first reverse-engineering app for macOS, Windows and Linux: load any app or binary and ask your AI agent what it does while it disassembles and analyzes the code for you.

name: Don't Be Michael
description: A free, open-source AI office for small businesses on Mac and Windows: pick your type of business, get a ready team of AI agents for each department, and a manager agent hands out the work and flags what needs you.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT).

name: Reason Network
description: A small peer-to-peer daemon that links coding-agent sessions across your team's computers, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents can see who is working on what and message each other directly, with no server.

name: Hy-Memory
description: Tencent Hunyuan's open-source memory system for agents that extracts, organizes and recalls long-term memories across sessions, with a memory hub and plugins for popular agent tools.

name: Firedrill
description: A simulation platform for testing AI agents before launch: it runs your agent through realistic scenarios with simulated users and tools, scores results against checks or rubrics and shows where it fails. Includes a remote MCP server.
pricing_detail: Free during early access (future pricing to be announced)

name: Kernel
description: Cloud browsers for AI agents: launch headless or live-view Chrome sessions in milliseconds with stealth mode, persistent profiles and replays, controlled through an API, CLI or MCP server. Free tier plus usage pricing.
pricing_detail: Free tier plus usage; Hobbyist $30/month, Start-up $200/month, Enterprise custom.

name: draw.io MCP
description: The official draw.io MCP server, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other assistants can create and edit flowcharts, architecture diagrams and other draw.io diagrams right in the chat. Free and needs no sign-in.
pricing_detail: Free; hosted MCP App server needs no sign-in.

name: BrowserStack MCP
description: BrowserStack's official MCP server, letting coding agents run manual and automated tests on real browsers and devices, debug failures and check accessibility from the IDE.
pricing_detail: From $12.50/mo; Live Team $150/mo billed yearly (5 users); free trial

name: Appwrite MCP
description: Appwrite's official MCP servers, so agents can manage Appwrite databases, users, storage and functions and look up Appwrite docs while building your backend.

name: Algolia MCP
description: Algolia's official MCP server that lets assistants search and manage Algolia indices, check analytics and tune relevance through natural-language requests.
pricing_detail: Requires Algolia: Grow from $0/mo (10K searches included), then usage; Enterprise

name: OneUptime MCP
description: OneUptime's official MCP server, giving agents access to monitors, incidents, on-call and status pages in this open-source observability platform. Free plan, paid plans from $22 per user, or self-host.
pricing_detail: OneUptime free plan; paid plans from $22 per user/month; self-host free.

name: Openlayer MCP
description: Openlayer's MCP server, letting coding agents pull evaluation results, failing tests and monitoring data from Openlayer so they can debug and improve AI systems from the IDE.
pricing_detail: Requires Openlayer: free Basic plan; Enterprise custom

name: Mapbox MCP
description: Mapbox's official MCP server that gives agents geocoding, directions, travel-time isochrones, points of interest and static map images through Mapbox APIs.

name: LaunchDarkly MCP
description: LaunchDarkly's official MCP server, so agents can create, update and clean up feature flags, AI configs and targeting rules from the IDE or chat.
pricing_detail: Requires LaunchDarkly: Developer $0/mo forever; pay as you go from $10/service connection/mo; Enterprise

name: Sanity MCP
description: Sanity's official remote MCP server that lets assistants query, create and update content, schemas and releases in a Sanity project using plain language.
pricing_detail: Requires Sanity: Free; Growth $15/seat/mo; Enterprise custom

name: Wabi
description: An AI assistant you use together with friends and family: plan a trip, book a stay or turn an inside joke into a quick game or mini-app, all in one shared space. On iPhone, Android and Mac.
pricing_detail: Free to download on iPhone, Android and Mac.

name: Zapia
description: A personal AI assistant on WhatsApp, iPhone, Android and the web that books, reminds, searches, compares prices and handles everyday errands for you. Free plan plus Pro and Ultra.
pricing_detail: Free plan; Pro and Ultra paid plans.

name: VisorBot
description: An Android automation app where you type or say a task and VisorBot taps, swipes and types through your apps to do it, with reusable recipes. Free plan; Plus from $4.99 a month.
pricing_detail: Free forever plan; Plus $4.99/month or $47.99/year; Pro available.

name: AgentBay
description: Alibaba Cloud's cloud sandbox service for agents, offering ready-made browser, Linux and Windows desktop, mobile and code environments that agents control through an SDK or MCP.
pricing_detail: Usage-based Alibaba Cloud billing; free trial available.

name: Paddle MCP
description: Paddle's official remote MCP server, so assistants can look up and manage products, prices, customers, subscriptions and transactions in your Paddle billing account.
pricing_detail: Requires Paddle: 5% + 50¢ per checkout transaction; custom pricing for high volume

name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
description: Microsoft's low-code platform for building, testing and publishing AI agents that connect to business data, Microsoft 365, Power Platform connectors and MCP servers, then deploy to Teams, websites and other channels.
pricing_detail: Copilot Studio $200 license (pre-purchase) or pay-as-you-go; free Azure account with $200 credit to start.

name: Sage
description: Sage is an open-source (MIT) RSI agent harness, where RSI stands for Recursive Self-Improvement: it improves agents using feedback from their tasks. Starting from a goal or a curated usage history, it runs the agent, has a separate evaluator grade the results, tunes the agent and keeps every version with its evidence, so you decide which one to adopt. It comes as a Desktop app, a multi-user Server with Agent Studio, and the SAgents Python runtime, with support for Skills, MCP, multi-agent setups and sandboxed runs with approvals.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); model-provider API usage is billed separately

name: CosVoice
description: CosVoice gives the AI assistant you already use (Grok Bot, ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor or any MCP client) a real US phone number in your area code and its own email address. It places and answers calls for you, such as booking a table or taking a contractor's quote, then sends a written summary and transcript to your inbox; connect it through its open-source (MIT) MCP server.
pricing_detail: Paid: $29/month after a 7-day free trial (card required; trial includes 10 minutes of calls); plan includes 100 call minutes a month

name: Hypit
description: An open-source agent workflow that takes a viral short video and rebuilds it as an editable template, letting you swap the presenter, script, voice and B-roll to produce many new variants with your own API keys.
pricing_detail: Free to use (no Hypit seat price or per-render fee). Modified Apache-2.0; model APIs you connect are billed separately.

name: opencodex
description: A local provider proxy that lets OpenAI Codex (CLI, app and SDK) and Claude Code run on other model providers such as Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek or local Ollama models.
pricing_detail: Open-source (MIT); see site for any hosted plans

name: Open Executive
description: A self-hostable virtual executive: one executive persona backed by a team of specialist agents that handle planning, research, communication and follow-ups for a founder or manager.

name: Weave Router
description: An open-source LLM router for Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents that sends each request to the cheapest model that still meets your quality bar, cutting model spend.

name: FuXi
description: A terminal AI coding agent that edits code, runs commands and works across 30+ model families, with parallel multi-provider inference and cost-aware model routing.
pricing_detail: Free Hobby plan with $15 usage credit; paid plans coming soon

name: OpenChatCut
description: A local-first AI video editor with a multi-track timeline that you drive by chatting with an agent; the AGPL edition is free, and a Pro desktop app adds transcription-based editing.

name: open-kritt
description: A self-hosted AI security research tool that orchestrates agents to hunt for vulnerabilities in a codebase and then validate and rank what they find; managed scans are also offered.

name: Memmy
description: A local-first personal AI agent with a self-evolving long-term memory that its desktop app, CLI and your other AI agents can all share.

name: nodeterm
description: A node-based terminal manager for macOS and Linux that shows real terminals and coding agents like Claude Code, Codex and Gemini as live nodes on an infinite canvas you can wire together.

name: AnySearch
description: A search MCP server and API for AI agents, covering real-time web search, vertical search and parallel batch queries with structured results and anonymous access.

name: Growth Lab
description: An open-source growth agent that learns your product, gathers data, researches the market, runs growth experiments and learns from the results to pick the next move.

name: Beacon
description: An open-source memory layer that captures traces from coding agents across harnesses and turns them into self-improving memory and visibility into what your agents did.

name: LCU
description: Brings the computer-use runtime from the ChatGPT desktop app to Claude Code, Codex CLI and Pi, so any agent harness can see and control your desktop without a Codex sign-in.

name: OpenOSINT
description: An open-source OSINT engine with about 20 passive investigation tools usable from a CLI, a web UI or an MCP server for AI assistants, with hosted monitoring and due-diligence plans.

name: Zero
description: An open-source terminal coding agent written in Go that works with 30+ model providers, supports MCP, skills and subagents, and keeps all sessions on your own disk.

name: ktx
description: An open-source context layer for data and analytics agents that gives Claude Code, Codex and other agents a self-improving map of your warehouse, metrics and business definitions.

name: Agentlas
description: A local-first agent OS that keeps specialist agents in a hub and spins up a temporary orchestrator for each task, with reusable methods and your choice of model and host.

name: OpenLore
description: A self-hosted knowledge repository for AI agents written in Go, where agents and teams share docs, notes and findings over SSH and MCP with scoped access.

name: Lody
description: A team workspace for running AI coding agents in parallel in isolated Git worktrees, with live diff review, GitHub integration and access from phone or desktop.

name: OpenMeld
description: An open-source collaboration system where people, cloud agents and coding agents such as Codex, Claude Code and Cursor share context and pick up each other's work.

name: AI Beat
description: An open-source AI red-teaming suite: PromptBeat attacks models and prompts, and AgentBeat runs black-box security evaluations against HTTP-exposed agents.

name: LiteLLM Agent Platform
description: A control plane from the LiteLLM team that gives one API and gateway for calling many agents, such as OpenCode, Claude Managed Agents, Cursor Agents and Deep Agents.

name: tty7
description: A terminal workbench whose shell sessions survive closing the app, built so coding agents can drive other agents' terminals and you can reattach remotely.

name: AgentDock (NexusDock)
description: A secure MCP runtime that lets ChatGPT, Claude and other AI clients operate your Mac, Windows, Linux and Android devices, with memory, tools and reusable automations.

name: thClaws
description: An open-source AI agent workspace in native Rust that runs locally as a GUI, CLI, headless service or web app from a single binary, with multiple model providers.

name: Ongrid
description: An ops agent that learns your infrastructure, finds the root cause of incidents and helps fix them from the chat apps your team already uses.

name: Tel-Agent
description: A self-hosted AI agent that answers phone calls and handles support on WhatsApp, Telegram, web chat and email with your own models and keys.

name: Caspian
description: An open-source communication SDK that lets AI agents send and receive messages over email, WhatsApp, Slack, Discord and other channels.

name: Repo Prompt
description: The community edition of Repo Prompt, a native macOS context-engineering app that packs the right files into prompts for AI coding work and exposes the same tools to agents via MCP.

name: ThinkRail
description: JetBrains' lightweight agentic IDE that pairs you with the pi coding agent, with isolated git-worktree workspaces, editor tabs, terminals and diffs.

name: agent-qa (Vostride)
description: A self-improving AI QA agent with persistent memory that tests web, Android and iOS apps from plain-English test steps, for developers and coding agents.

name: GoRaven
description: A self-hosted AI agent platform for teams where agents read files, run code, call APIs and work through tasks instead of just chatting.

name: Xyne
description: Juspay's open-source enterprise AI platform for building apps and agents on top of your company's own context, model-agnostic and self-hostable.

name: AutoScientists
description: A research system from Harvard's Zitnik lab where teams of LLM agents self-organize to plan and run long-running scientific experiments.

name: AgentConnect
description: An open-source, multi-agent workspace where you @-mention any agent wherever work happens, and agents work alongside your team and each other.

name: hax
description: A minimalist terminal coding agent shipped as a single native C binary using a few MB of RAM, with first-class local models plus OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter support.

name: projectmem
description: A local-first memory layer for coding agents that records issues, attempts, fixes and decisions and warns your agent before it repeats a past mistake.

name: KiwiFS
description: A markdown filesystem for agents and teams: searchable, structured and versioned knowledge in a single binary that agents can read and write.

name: CozyClay
description: Free browser-based 3D previs software: block a scene, pose characters and author camera moves and cuts, then hand the same shots to an AI video model.

name: luvus
description: Mission control for AI coding agents: run, watch, resume and orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, opencode and others from one terminal with a live view of each agent.

name: Second Brain
description: A free, open-source shared memory that runs in your own Cloudflare account, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP clients can recall the same projects, preferences and decisions.

name: ai-memory
description: Fabio Akita's open-source long-term memory layer for coding agents: one Rust binary that keeps plain-markdown project memory and typed handoffs shared across 20+ harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI, so you can switch agents, machines or teammates without re-explaining the project.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); you pay only for the coding agents and models you already use

name: Dodaios
description: Open-source desktop agent OS for Windows, macOS and Linux (formerly Personal Jarvis): talk to it and it runs your coding CLIs side by side, your browser and your apps, with offline Whisper speech, a local wiki memory and support for Ollama, Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); works with a local model or an existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription, no API key required

name: OpenCity Record
description: OpenCity Record makes US city council and planning meetings searchable in plain language: what was decided, who voted and what is coming up, drawn from meeting transcripts, agendas and ordinances across hundreds of cities. Connect it to Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor through its remote MCP server and ask questions about your local government, with every answer citing the meeting it came from.
pricing_detail: Freemium: Free plan covers one city forever (speakers unattributed, 1,000 credits a month, no card); paid plans from $9/month (Resident, 3 cities) up to $499/month (Premium, all states); new accounts get full Premium free during the beta, until at least January 1, 2027

name: RoverLead
description: RoverLead is an AI SDR for LinkedIn. Its signal agents watch engagement around your niche, competitors and the experts your buyers follow to find in-market leads that match your ideal customer profile, then write a personalised opener from the exact signal and run outreach and follow-ups at LinkedIn-safe pacing. A shared inbox sorts replies by intent and drafts answers in your voice, and nothing goes out until you approve it. Connects to your CRM and to Claude or ChatGPT through MCP.
pricing_detail: Paid: 7-day free trial with no card; Starter $149/month per user (5,000 credits), Growth $449/month per user (25,000 credits, up to 10 signal agents), Enterprise custom

name: TypeSafe Jev
description: Jev is TypeSafe's System One decision model, built for the small decisions inside software and agents. You send a state and typed questions (choice, score and more) and get typed answers with probabilities back instead of free-form text, so code can branch on them directly to route, classify, score or rank options. Agents can use it to settle narrow calls cheaply and save the larger LLM for open-ended work. Available through TypeSafe's API, Python and JavaScript SDKs, an agent skill, and OpenRouter.
pricing_detail: Usage-based: pay per input token, output free; Jev 1.14 listed at $0.042 per million input tokens in TypeSafe docs; also on OpenRouter; enterprise plans via sales

name: Grok Bot Jev Router
description: Grok Bot Jev Router is an open-source Python reference router that puts TypeSafe Jev in front of Grok Bot as a cheap decision layer. Before expensive research, browser, retry or subagent work, Jev classifies the request and returns an explicit action such as reuse a cached result, stop a failing retry, cap research, run a deterministic step, or ask a human. It starts in shadow mode that only logs decisions, has an active mode for a Grok Bot skill that honors them, and includes a kill switch. It never sends, pays or deletes anything itself.
pricing_detail: Open source (MIT); needs a TypeSafe API key (Jev is billed per input token)

name: wren-guard Pro
description: wren-guard Pro is a TypeScript guard library for AI agents that hold or move funds on Base and other EVM chains (viem, CDP AgentKit, Privy, Eliza and similar stacks). It enforces allowlisted, capped and simulated sends, decodes calldata and signatures to flag unlimited approvals, Permit, Permit2, setApprovalForAll and EIP-7702 delegation, screens for injected instructions and watches nonces. It ships with an 89-scenario attack corpus drawn from public agent wallet incidents and a GitHub Action that fails CI if your agent's policy would let a known attack through. The original Python wren-guard is free and MIT licensed.
pricing_detail: Paid: one-off digital download, pay what you want at $19, $49 or $99 in USDC on Base (same files at every price); $0.01 sample over x402; the original Python wren-guard is free (MIT)

name: Wren x402 Doctor
description: Wren x402 Doctor helps sellers of x402 pay-per-call endpoints, the payment standard AI agents use to pay for APIs in USDC, get listed in the Coinbase CDP Bazaar and stay listed. A free lint checks a 402 response against the x402 v2 spec and the Bazaar listing rules (networks, amounts, payTo checksum, description length, injection-like text, schema and metadata), plus a seller's OpenAPI and x402 discovery documents. Paid endpoints include a Bazaar health check ($0.10) returning every listing for a wallet with 30-day calls, unique payers and estimated delisting dates; a market check (GET /market, $0.02) returning up to 20 comparable live listings with price quartiles; and GET /trust ($0.01), which traces who funds the wallets that pay an x402 seller using a weekly Base funding trace (splitting calls across seller-funded wallets, shared funders, multi-seller callers and independent wallets).
pricing_detail: Freemium: free lint of any 402 response and discovery documents; Bazaar health check $0.10, market check (GET /market) $0.02, and payer funding trace (GET /trust) $0.01 in USDC on Base per report over x402

name: The Commons (Dead Brands Collab Hub)
description: The Commons is an open discussion hub for AI agents and bots, run as a remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP) by Dead Brands. Agents can read rooms, threads, search and bot profiles anonymously, and post, reply, upvote and send presence heartbeats with a free, instant hub key they claim themselves through the hub_register tool. Rooms include introductions, lobby, build-log, help-desk and meta, with public moderation, newcomer rate limits and an AI judge that holds prompt-injection bait aimed at visiting bots.
pricing_detail: Free: open hub with free, self-serve hub keys; server code MIT licensed

name: Moltgate
description: Moltgate helps AI agent builders and automation operators turn agent ideas into paid offers. You package an agent workflow or automation as a fixed-price task with clear scope, deliverable and timing, publish it on a public profile and directory, and buyers pay by card to submit requests. Analytics show which offers sell, and paid requests can be routed to Claude Code, Codex, n8n, Zapier or your own agent through a REST API (polling) or webhooks, so repeat work can be automated.
pricing_detail: Freemium: Free plan publishes 1 offer at $9/$19/$29 task prices (you keep 80%); Pro $29/month (3 offers, $49/$99 prices, webhooks, analytics, keep 90%); Ultra $99/month (5 offers, up to $299 prices, keep 95%)

name: iArt
description: iArt is an AI motion graphics agent that turns a text prompt, or uploaded images, PDFs, slide decks, audio or a web link, into animated scenes. It writes real animation code scene by scene (layout, typography, timing, transitions), so text stays exactly spelled and you can refine the result by chatting ("make the title two seconds shorter"). It handles explainers, logo animations, kinetic typography, animated charts, lower thirds and audio-synced captions, adds AI voiceover or a cloned voice, and exports MP4 (1080p on Pro, 4K on Ultra) or transparent WebM overlays.
pricing_detail: Freemium: Free plan with a $2 signup credit (watermarked, share links); Pro $20/month ($30 monthly credit, 1080p, no watermark, 3 cloned voices); Ultra $50/month ($80 monthly credit, 4K, 10 cloned voices); 20% off yearly

name: Wren Pre-sign Check
description: Wren Pre-sign Check is a pay-per-call x402 API that an AI agent calls before it signs anything with its wallet. Send a transaction (to + data), an EIP-712 typed-data payload or untrusted text, and it returns block, review or allow, the decoded call in plain words and every finding: unlimited approvals, Permit and Permit2 signatures, setApprovalForAll, EIP-7702 delegation, contract deployment and injected instructions. With an optional wren-guard policy (allowlist, spenders, caps) it also blocks unknown recipients, over-cap amounts and lookalike addresses. It is a static check and stores nothing you send; free demos show real output.
pricing_detail: Paid: $0.01 in USDC on Base per check over x402 (EIP-3009 payment authorisation, no approvals); free demo endpoints with fixed examples

name: OpenKnowledge
description: OpenKnowledge is a free, local-first markdown editor and knowledge base built for working alongside AI agents. It looks and feels like a Notion-style WYSIWYG editor, with callouts, tabs, Mermaid diagrams and media blocks, but every page stays a plain markdown file on your disk. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and dozens of others can read and write the same files through its integrations, so specs, team wikis and LLM wikis stay in one place that both people and agents keep up to date. It ships as a desktop app plus a web UI and CLI.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (GPL-3.0): desktop app, web UI and CLI

name: Cumora
description: Cumora is a team chat app where AI agents are members of the workspace rather than a chat box you prompt. Each agent gets a persona, its own private memory and files, a status, and a schedule on which it wakes up, reads the room and decides whether to message someone, post an idea or pull a small group together. Agents can message each other, and you can read those side conversations. People join by email or link, agents can be grouped into teams and given projects, and the same live workspace runs on desktop, in the browser and on a phone. It is free during an invite-only preview.
pricing_detail: Free during the invite-only preview; open source (MIT); macOS, Windows, Linux, web and phone

name: MonoCode
description: MonoCode is a desktop app that puts the coding agents you already pay for behind one interface. It drives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, Pi, Hermes Agent, Devin and others, using the subscriptions and logins already on your machine, so you never buy tokens through it. Each tab is an agent session and one composer sends work to whichever agent you pick, so several sessions can run side by side. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, with an iOS app in public beta.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); uses your existing agent subscriptions, sells no tokens

name: PR Lens
description: PR Lens helps people review code that agents wrote. For each pull request it draws animated architecture and data-flow diagrams inside the PR, showing which parts of the app were added, changed or removed, what else depends on the change and how a request now moves through the system. It also flags likely bugs, security holes and design problems in the same review comment, with a ready prompt to hand each fix to your coding agent or an autofix. The open-source core runs locally and installs as an agent skill.
pricing_detail: Open-source core (MIT), runs locally; installs as an agent skill

name: OpenAPPA
description: OpenAPPA is a deterministic guardrail that sits between an AI agent and its tools and tracks how data flows across tool calls, instead of asking a second model to judge each call. Policies decide whether untrusted or sensitive data may reach a given action, which blocks data exfiltration caused by prompt injection or hallucination while letting agents finish their tasks. It plugs into Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, kAgent and Archestra, comes with reusable policy "batteries", validation, observability and reporting, and is backed by a NeurIPS workshop paper with published benchmarks. It is in preview as an open RFC.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); preview and RFC

name: Hermex
description: Hermex is a native iPhone and iPad app for controlling a self-hosted Hermes agent. The agent keeps running on your own server; the app connects to it over your private Tailscale network or an HTTPS tunnel, streams replies, lets you answer approval requests, manage tasks and Kanban boards, browse the agent's workspace and get push notifications when it needs you. It is free on the App Store with no in-app purchases, and its source is open.
pricing_detail: Free on the App Store, no in-app purchases; open source (MIT); needs your own Hermes server

name: Wake
description: Wake is a desktop app that collects every coding-agent conversation on your computer into one searchable place. It reads the local history kept by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Devin and other agents, groups sessions by agent and project, and lets you find a past conversation in seconds and resume it in your terminal. It is read-only and nothing leaves your machine. Built in Rust, it runs on macOS, with Linux and Windows in beta.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); macOS 14+, Linux and Windows beta

name: Superlog
description: Superlog runs AI agents on routine engineering work around production. You set up automations with triggers and connectors, for example rating each new Sentry issue, posting a plain-language summary to Slack and opening a pull request with the fix, comparing error rates and latency against their normal range every hour, adding missing logs and spans to hard-to-debug code paths, or answering community questions from your code and docs. You choose the model and agent harness and bring your own tokens or subscriptions. The core is open source (Apache-2.0) with a hosted version.
pricing_detail: Open source (Apache-2.0) to self-host; hosted plans and enterprise on the pricing page; bring your own model tokens or subscriptions

name: IDA MCP (Hex-Rays)
description: IDA MCP is Hex-Rays' official MCP server for the IDA disassembler and decompiler. It lets AI coding agents and people work on the same IDA databases at the same time, so an agent can inspect functions, types and decompiled code, rename and annotate, and coordinate analysis across several related binaries in one session. It works with the IDA GUI through a plugin or headless through idalib, installs with Hex-Rays' hcli tool, and needs IDA 9.4 or later.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); requires a licensed IDA 9.4 or later

name: LayerFS
description: LayerFS is a filesystem built for running many coding agents in parallel. Each agent mounts a complete, writable workspace on top of shared committed history, does its work, commits what it changed and goes away, so compute only exists while a command runs. Every tool call becomes a commit on a branch, same-file clashes between agents are refused rather than silently merged, each line records the step that wrote it, and any commit can be forked at no cost for recursive exploration or RL training. Agents on different computers share one serverless store with chunk-level deduplication.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT)

name: Co-op Anything
description: Co-op Anything lets you point your AI coding agent at a single-player game and have it build or revive a co-op mod, so you can play it with friends online or split-screen. The project gives the agent a step-by-step method for working out what has to be synced between players (the story, enemies, the world, items and players seeing each other) and testing it. Its website is a searchable directory of every co-op mod made this way, with player ratings, how much of each game works in co-op and how active each project is.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT)

name: Tov
description: Tov is an experimental programming language designed to be written by coding agents. It uses TypeScript syntax minus a few traps (no any, null or loose equality, separate int and float types, and failing calls marked with try), so agents already know how to write it, and its compiler returns machine-readable fixes the agent can apply after every edit. Programs compile to small, fast native binaries, with published benchmarks against Rust, Bun and Node. Agents can learn it from the site's llms.txt.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); experimental v0.0.1

name: Concat
description: Concat is a free, open-source video editor meant as a CapCut replacement that runs entirely on your own machine. It covers auto-captions, text-to-speech voices, background removal, keyframes, titles, effects, filters and transitions with multi-track editing up to 4K, with no watermark, account or subscription. It runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, and it can be scripted through a documented JSON-RPC and gRPC API, so scripts and AI agents can drive edits.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (AGPL-3.0); no watermark, account or subscription

name: onetake
description: onetake is an agent skill for Claude Code and similar agents that makes product launch films, teasers and feature demos as one continuous camera move, where each beat grows out of the previous one instead of cutting between slides. The agent writes the motion as code and renders it with ffmpeg, and the skill checks continuity at every transition. The free edition on GitHub is for noncommercial use; onetake Pro adds a camera operator that follows each beat, source files for every example film, starter templates and a commercial licence.
pricing_detail: Free edition on GitHub (PolyForm Noncommercial); onetake Pro $79 one time with a commercial licence and all 1.x updates

name: OpenComputer
description: OpenComputer is a platform for building and deploying long-running AI agents as code. You define an agent as a TypeScript function with its model, tools and MCP servers, deploy it with one command, and every session gets its own real cloud computer, with managed sessions, schedules and API keys kept outside the agent's runtime. Templates include a coding agent that edits a repo, runs checks and opens a draft pull request, and market-research and GTM agents; its own Slack coding agent runs on it. Pricing is pay-as-you-go for model calls and per-second machine time.
pricing_detail: Pay as you go (model calls at API rates, machine time per second, $10 free credit); Pro $20/mo and Max $200/mo prepaid credit at 10x; Enterprise custom. Core is open source (Apache-2.0)

name: Fish Audio
description: Fish Audio is a voice AI platform for text to speech, voice cloning and speech to text, with a real-time API for voice agents. Its Drama 3 and S2 models take inline emotion and delivery tags such as whispering, laughing or pauses, it can clone a voice from a few seconds of audio, and its library has more than two million community voices for narration, characters, audiobooks and support agents. The Fish Speech models behind it are published on GitHub and Hugging Face.
pricing_detail: Free tier (8,000 credits a month); Plus $11/mo and Pro $75/mo billed yearly ($15 and $100 monthly); Max $749/mo yearly; API billed by usage

name: LVLZ
description: LVLZ is a personal AI agent you run by messaging it like a person, on iMessage or WhatsApp, as a text, voice note or call. It runs errands on real websites in a cloud browser, such as bookings, forms and shopping, turns messages into tasks and projects, fills a CRM from your conversations, and runs routines like a morning brief or a price watch. Everything it does lands in a web workspace, its memory can be read, edited and exported, and it asks before paying, contacting someone new or deleting anything, with cards and passwords kept in an encrypted vault.
pricing_detail: Personal $19/mo, Pro $49/mo, Business $149/mo, each with a 7-day free trial

name: Sundae
description: Sundae is a personal AI assistant you text from iMessage or Android RCS, with no app or account needed. It works on a computer of its own: it books tables, finds flights at current prices, compares shops, reads letters and photos you send, sets reminders, watches prices and builds simple web pages, then texts back with a screenshot so you can check. It remembers what you tell it, asks before spending money, sending, deleting or opening accounts, and stops at checkout for you to pay. It is free to start with a daily limit, with a paid Plus plan, and is in limited beta.
pricing_detail: Free to start with a daily limit; paid Plus plan raises it; limited beta

name: WaveSpeed MCP
description: WaveSpeed MCP is WaveSpeedAI's official MCP server and CLI, which lets an AI agent run any model in WaveSpeed's live catalog of over a thousand image, video, audio and 3D generation models from one connection. Agents can pick a model, submit a generation job and get the result back without switching tools. It is available as a hosted remote server or a local install, and usage is billed per generation at WaveSpeed's API prices.
pricing_detail: Pay per generation at WaveSpeed API prices; eligible new accounts get $1 free credit; MCP server is open source

name: trivago MCP
description: trivago MCP is trivago's official remote MCP server for hotel search. Ask an AI assistant about a destination, dates and guests, and it returns live hotel prices compared across hundreds of booking sites in one tool call, with a map widget in ChatGPT. It needs no API key and connects in about a minute to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and any client that reads the MCP Registry.
pricing_detail: Free, no API key

name: Sphinx
description: Open-source Git hook for agent-assisted coding: before code your agent wrote is pushed to a protected branch, it reads the diff and quizzes you on what the change actually does when things go wrong, and only lets the push through once you answer correctly. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); questions are generated by a model you choose (your existing coding agent, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), so you pay only for those tokens

name: Reticle
description: Verification layer for AI coding agents: a dev-only SDK inside your web or desktop app lets the agent drive real flows and read network calls, app state and console, then returns a pass, fail or cannot-tell verdict with the file and line to fix; saved flows replay without an AI model and can gate CI.
pricing_detail: Embeddable SDK packages are Apache-2.0; the server, init and test packages are FSL-1.1-ALv2 (free for internal use, Apache-2.0 after two years); the hosted platform at app.reticle.sh is free to start with no credit card; enterprise features need a paid licence (price not listed publicly)

name: Bidhelm
description: Bidhelm is your AI marketing department. It runs your ads and posts to your X profile. Live on Google Ads and your X profile today. From $79 a month. Start 14 days free. Cancel anytime.
pricing_detail: From $79/month; 14-day free trial, cancel anytime

name: ClipTalk
description: ClipTalk is an AI video agent that makes finished short-form videos for TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. Give it a prompt, script, product, website, photo or link and it writes the script, generates the visuals, adds a voiceover from 140+ AI voices in 30+ languages, word-by-word captions, B-roll and music, then renders a ready-to-post MP4. You can edit any scene by asking in plain language, clone your own voice, cast AI characters, and on Pro use its API and MCP access for Claude and ChatGPT.
pricing_detail: Freemium: 50 free credits to start, no card needed (free-plan videos carry a watermark); paid plans (Starter, Pro, Ultra) from $39/month as listed on its pricing page, with the AI agent, API and MCP access on Pro

name: Fireply AI
description: Fireply is an AI agent for growing on X (Twitter): it finds relevant conversations in your niche and writes and posts context-aware replies in your own voice, so you can grow followers, reach and sales without replying by hand. Sign-in uses X OAuth, so it never sees your password, and it also offers free X tools like an account analyzer and advanced search.
pricing_detail: Freemium: 40 free replies to start, no card needed; paid plans from $69/month (Growth) as listed on its site, with a yearly option at about 20% off

name: Akeru Bot
description: Open-source alternative to Grok Bot for named AI teammates: local-first desktop, web and mobile clients where each bot has its own tools, instructions and memory. MIT-licensed independent fork of T3 Code.

name: Guaca
description: Desktop workspace inspired by Grok Bot where AI agents collaborate, write code and use tools; runs locally or on your own server, with shared conversations, persistent memory and MCP plugins. AGPL-3.0.

name: GoPlus Security MCP
description: GoPlus's MCP server that lets agents check token, address, NFT, approval and phishing-site risk before they act, using the GoPlus security API.
pricing_detail: Open source (Apache-2.0); GoPlus API has a free public tier
status_note: No recent updates: the GitHub repository has had no commits since May 2025 (checked Oct 25, 2026). It may still work, but expect little or no maintenance.

name: Tanod
description: Hosted security MCP and API for agents: pre-transaction checks for token honeypots, risky contracts, phishing URLs, OFAC sanctions, address poisoning, live approvals and wallet drains.
pricing_detail: Pay per call via x402 (from $0.001); 10 free chain reads a day

name: CoinGraph Wallet Guard
description: Checks a swap or send before you sign it: token contract risks, price impact, sanctioned or look-alike recipients. Returns SAFE, WARN or STOP via API or MCP.
pricing_detail: 1,000 free credits a month with an API key; MCP free during preview; x402 per call

name: Antalpha Wallet Guard
description: Open-source agent skill that scans EVM wallets for dangerous approvals, malicious addresses, risky tokens and NFTs, rug pulls and phishing sites, powered by GoPlus data.
pricing_detail: Open-source agent skill (MIT per README) on Antalpha's hosted MCP

name: Webacy
description: Risk ratings API and MCP server for wallets, tokens, vaults and transactions, so agents can screen addresses and check risk before moving funds.

name: ScamSniffer
description: Real-time intelligence on phishing sites, wallet drainers and scammer addresses: a free browser extension plus a blocklist API teams and agents can query.
pricing_detail: Free browser extension; blocklist API plans from $84/mo

name: De.Fi Scanner
description: Smart-contract and token scanner that flags honeypots, owner powers and other contract risks, with a credit-based API for apps and agents.
pricing_detail: Free web scanner; API uses paid credits

name: Dune MCP
description: Dune's official remote MCP server: agents search on-chain datasets, write and run DuneSQL, fetch results and build charts across 100+ chains.
pricing_detail: Free plan; paid plans add credits (14-day trial)

name: GoldRush MCP
description: Covalent's GoldRush multichain data API with an MCP server, giving agents wallet balances, transactions, token and NFT data across 100+ chains.
pricing_detail: 14-day free trial, then from $10/mo; x402 pay per request

name: Helius MCP
description: Helius's MCP server for Solana: agents read accounts, transactions, tokens and NFTs through Helius RPC and APIs.
pricing_detail: Free plan; paid plans on site

name: Santiment
description: Crypto market intelligence on on-chain, social and development activity, with an AI assistant and API that agents can use for research.
pricing_detail: Free plan; Sanbase Pro from $49/mo

name: thirdweb Nebula
description: thirdweb's AI for onchain work: agents read live chain data, analyze transactions and can buy, swap and send crypto from connected wallets.
pricing_detail: Free tier; usage-based beyond

name: Coinbase Agentic Wallet MCP
description: Coinbase's MCP server and wallet app (formerly Payments MCP) that let agents hold USDC and pay for x402 services on Base, Polygon and Solana within spend limits you set.
status_note: No recent updates: the GitHub repository has had no commits since Oct 2025 (checked Oct 25, 2026). It may still work, but expect little or no maintenance.

name: Alby MCP
description: Open-source MCP server that connects a Bitcoin Lightning wallet to your agent via Nostr Wallet Connect, so it can pay and create invoices.
pricing_detail: Open source (Apache-2.0)

name: Forta Firewall
description: Forta's pre-execution firewall that screens transactions for exploits and malicious activity and can block them before they settle onchain.

name: Bitquery MCP
description: Bitquery's hosted, read-only MCP server with 300+ tools for DEX trades, candles, wallet history and money-flow tracing across 40+ chains.
pricing_detail: Free tier with a Bitquery account; metered on your plan

name: The Graph Token API MCP
description: The Graph's Token API MCP server that lets agents query token metadata, balances, transfers and holder stats in plain language.
pricing_detail: Available on all tiers, including free
status_note: No recent updates: the GitHub repository has had no commits since Mar 2025 (checked Oct 25, 2026). It may still work, but expect little or no maintenance.

name: Messari Copilot
description: Blockworks AI (formerly Messari Copilot) is an AI research copilot for crypto, answering questions from Blockworks Research and Messari research, news and market data, with an API and hosted MCP server for agents.
pricing_detail: Enterprise plan (Messari moved to Blockworks AI); Copilot API also pay-per-request via x402

name: Blockaid
description: Onchain security platform used by wallets and exchanges: transaction simulation and scanning that blocks malicious dApps, tokens and signatures before users or agents sign.

name: Moralis MCP
description: Moralis's MCP server that gives agents wallet, token, NFT and DeFi data across EVM chains and Solana in plain language.
pricing_detail: Free plan; paid plans on site

name: Playable Notes
description: Playable Notes is an AI music tool for piano teachers: snap a photo, screenshot or PDF of piano sheet music and it reads it into a real, playable score, then rearranges it for your student from a plain-language request like "easier left hand", "take out the octaves" or "put it in C". You can hear it, fix any note, print a clean PDF and share practice links, and it also works inside ChatGPT.
pricing_detail: Freemium: 50 free credits on sign-up (1 credit reads one line of music) and editing, AI arranging (up to 100 a day), playback and printing are free; credit packs from $10 for 100 credits, as listed on its site
good_for: Piano teachers adapting sheet music for students

name: Metix AI
description: Metix AI (formerly OpenJobs AI) is an AI recruiting platform built around Mira, an AI recruiter agent: you describe the role and Mira searches 900M+ profiles in 190+ countries, runs personalized outreach only after you approve it, handles replies and screening, and books interview-ready candidates on your calendar, often within 24 hours. You still approve outreach and run the interviews.
pricing_detail: Paid: free 14-day trial (1 AI Agent and 500 Credits, no card required), then subscription plans from $99/month (Starter, 5,000 Credits and 1 AI Agent) up to Scale at $499/month, plus a Delivery service; prices as listed on its site

name: GMapsScraper.AI
description: GMapsScraper.AI is an AI-powered Google Maps scraper for lead generation: enter keywords and it pulls business listings with names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, social links, ratings, reviews, photos and opening hours, exported to CSV or JSON. It also offers a REST API and a remote MCP server (/api/mcp) so AI agents in Claude, Cursor or OpenAI can run Google Maps searches directly.
pricing_detail: Freemium: free plan with 1,000 credits per month (1 credit = 1 business), then Starter $29/month (50,000 credits), Pro $99/month (300,000) and Business $199/month (1,000,000), plus on-demand credits from $15 per 15,000; prices as listed on its site

name: superagnt
description: superagnt is a marketing plugin for Claude and ChatGPT that helps businesses find customers through outbound, SEO and ads. With it, your AI can find the people worth reaching and load them into your outbound, see what you and your competitors rank for, and see the ads your competitors run.
pricing_detail: Paid: free 7-day trial with no card ($3 of data credits and Growth limits), then Starter $49/month, Growth $149/month or Scale $399/month, each with monthly data credits included; Enterprise is custom; prices as listed on its site

name: Claude Duet
description: Claude Duet is Anthropic's proactive personal agent app, in research preview. You message it like an assistant: it sends a morning brief from your connected apps, keeps watch on your inbox, calendar and follow-ups through the day, and only pings you when something needs you. You can also hand it tasks, from scheduling meetings to building dashboards or simple web apps, and it keeps working when you step away but checks with you before acting on your behalf. It runs on iOS, Android and claude.ai, starting with a waitlist for US Pro and Max subscribers on their existing plan limits.
pricing_detail: Research preview by waitlist for US Pro and Max plans

name: 1Password for Agents
description: 1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents sign in to your accounts without ever seeing your passwords or one-time codes. When a supported agent reaches a sign-in page, it asks for a credential from your vault; you approve the request, and 1Password fills it straight into the site, so the secret never enters the model or its memory. You can see and manage which agents have access to what. It launched with integrations for agents such as Claude Duet, ChatGPT Work and dots, Meta's Muse and Grok Bot, and needs a 1Password plan.
pricing_detail: Included with 1Password plans

name: PhoneUse
description: PhoneUse gives AI agents phones of their own to operate. Agents get cloud Android phones that boot in seconds and scale to hundreds, or real retail iPhones and Androids in a San Francisco rack, tapped by a robot stylus, for apps that detect emulators, with real carrier numbers for SMS and 2FA codes. One MCP server with tools such as acquire, read screen, tap, type, swipe, open app and read SMS plugs into Claude, Cursor, Codex or Windsurf, and there is a Python SDK and REST API. On-demand cloud phones are billed per minute, with flat monthly prices for dedicated and real phones.
pricing_detail: Cloud phones $0.30 per minute on demand; dedicated and real phones monthly

name: Needle
description: Needle is an outbound engine built for AI agents to drive. You connect it to Claude, ChatGPT or Grok and describe who you want to reach in one prompt; it finds leads from LinkedIn, Instagram and Google Maps, enriches them with context for personal messages, and reaches out from your own connected accounts on whichever channel the lead uses, with sending limits built in. It works for sales, partnerships, hiring or fundraising outreach, and you can start for free.
pricing_detail: Free to start; paid plans

name: BAND
description: BAND is an interaction layer for teams running many AI agents alongside people. Agents and humans share one chat-like workspace where they coordinate tasks, exchange context and hand off work in real time, with governance over how agents communicate built in, instead of hand-wiring every handoff. BAND for Developers connects coding agents across your existing development tools so they can work together without you acting as their project manager.

name: UseIt Studio
description: UseIt Studio is an AI design agent for things you can hold. You describe what you want in a sentence, it asks the questions a designer would, and you refine any detail by pointing at it. Instead of a flat mockup you get a real, editable design file ready to print, cut and fold, with true dimensions, bleed and dielines, for pins, stickers, gift boxes, pop-up cards, packaging and brand kits. It runs in the browser, and a Windows desktop helper lets you call it up anywhere.
pricing_detail: Free to try; paid plans

name: Voxtral 3
description: Voxtral 3 is Mistral AI's voice agent stack: speech-to-text in 50+ languages with speaker labels and end-of-turn detection, expressive text-to-speech in 35+ languages, and a voice agent SDK built on LiveKit that handles listening, tool calls and speaking in one stream over SIP or WebRTC. You can use it through Mistral's API with EU, US or global endpoints, or deploy it yourself, and it is priced per minute of audio or per character.
pricing_detail: Transcription from $0.0035/min, TTS $13 per 1M characters, voice agent API from $0.04/min

name: Mercury 3
description: Mercury 3 is Inception's diffusion language model, which writes many tokens in parallel rather than one at a time, reaching over 1,000 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs with a 1M-token context, tool calling and structured outputs. It has an OpenAI-compatible API and is also offered on OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel, which makes it a fit for voice bots, support agents and browser agents where response speed matters. Pricing is per million input and output tokens.
pricing_detail: $0.20 / $0.70 per million input / output tokens

name: OmniRush
description: OmniRush is a desktop coding agent for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a terminal CLI as well. It works through the files of your own projects, reading code, making edits and running commands, and gives free access to frontier models from a model picker, with GPT 6 Astra as the default. Builds for each platform are published on its releases page.
pricing_detail: Free desktop app with free frontier-model access

name: Unreal Agent
description: Unreal Agent is an async-first agent harness from Unreal Labs, a team researching how to make agentic workflows efficient. The library handles inputs with stable IDs and deduplication, append-only sessions that can be forked, and a coordinator that manages each model turn and translates tool calls into operations. It ships with a cloud agent runner, a terminal UI and benchmark runners, under the MIT license.

name: MemoraX Code
description: MemoraX Code is a shared memory layer for coding agents such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Trae and DeepSeek Harness. It recalls prior engineering knowledge, captures lessons from finished work, keeps repository knowledge and architecture history up to date, and carries your procedures and preferences into new sessions, bringing back only the memory relevant to the task at hand. It needs Node.js 20 or later and is MIT licensed.

name: AOCI-CODE
description: AOCI-CODE keeps a persistent, Git-versioned map of your whole codebase and database schema that your coding agent writes and a local MCP server governs. Agents in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor or OpenCode read the map once and know what each file is for, what it depends on and what must not break, instead of re-reading the repo on every task. It can index an existing codebase of up to about half a million lines and report how well it knows each area before taking over development.

name: OpenHarness
description: OpenHarness from Autonomous is a native command center for running coding agents side by side, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Devin, Amp and Copilot. It links your laptop, home server and GPU box into one window with a password instead of SSH keys or port forwarding, keeps code and keystrokes end-to-end encrypted through its relay, and is keyboard first. Agents keep working when you close it, and it extends beyond code to CAD, circuits, robots, games and music.

name: Wisp Science
description: Wisp Science is an open-source, local-first AI research workbench for scientists on Windows, macOS and Linux. Its agent searches the literature, runs persistent Python and R kernels on your laptop or remote servers, queries about 80 scientific databases and loads reusable skills, while keeping figures, runs, decisions and drafts together in one project. You bring your own OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic model, or drive Codex or Claude Code, and approval gates stay on by default.

name: Foreman
description: Foreman from ThruWire supervises coding agents with fast decision models. You give it a ticket, spec or bug report and it runs Codex, OpenCode, Hermes or LangChain's Deep Agents Code as workers, or attaches to supported sessions such as Pi, then independently judges whether the job meets the original requirements, whether the test evidence is enough and when verification or human input is needed. Extra checks can be configured for your workflow, and it is MIT licensed.

name: FableCut
description: FableCut is a Premiere-style video editor that runs entirely in the browser and exposes the whole timeline as one JSON document, covering media, clips, tracks, effects, keyframes and transitions. You can edit by hand or let an AI agent such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop cut the video over MCP or REST while the timeline updates live. It has no npm dependencies, starts with one node command and is MIT licensed.

name: Diagrid Catalyst MCP
description: The Diagrid Catalyst MCP server lets AI coding agents build and operate Dapr Workflows and Dapr durable agents on Diagrid Catalyst, the managed platform for long-running, fault-tolerant agent and workflow apps. Through it an agent can create and inspect workflows, check running instances and manage Catalyst resources from your MCP client. It is the official server from Diagrid, the company behind Dapr, and needs a Catalyst sign-in.

name: Cayu
description: Cayu is an open-source Python framework for building and running domain-specific, long-horizon agents on a durable runtime. Sessions survive restarts and redeploys from SQLite or Postgres stores, tool policies can require human approval before side effects, spend caps are checked before each model call, and timers, background tasks, subagents and forks cover longer multi-agent work. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.

name: Inngest
description: Inngest is a durable workflow orchestration platform for running stateful step functions and AI workflows on serverless, servers or the edge. You write functions in TypeScript, Python or Go with automatic retries, queues, throttling and human-in-the-loop waits, and its AgentKit and AI inference steps let you build durable, long-running AI agents with tracing and evals. The server is source-available (SSPL, converting to Apache 2.0 later) and can be self-hosted, or you can use Inngest Cloud.
pricing_detail: Inngest Cloud: Free $0/mo (50k executions, 5 seats), Pro $99/mo, Business $499/mo, Enterprise custom (inngest.com/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026). Server is source-available (SSPL with delayed Apache 2.0) and self-hostable.

name: Windmill
description: Windmill is an open-source developer platform that turns scripts in Python, TypeScript, Go, SQL and other languages into webhooks, workflows and internal UIs. Its flows include AI agent steps that call an LLM with your scripts as tools, support nested agents and MCP, and run on a fast self-hostable workflow engine. It positions itself as an open-source alternative to Retool and Temporal.
pricing_detail: Free and open-source Community Edition from $0/mo (self-hosted, unlimited executions, up to 10 SSO users); Enterprise from $120/mo; cloud and self-hosted paid plans (windmill.dev/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026). Core is AGPLv3, some enterprise features proprietary.

name: Kestra
description: Kestra is an open-source, event-driven orchestration and scheduling platform where workflows are declared in YAML or built in a no-code editor. It includes an AI Agent task that gives flows an LLM with memory and tools, supports nested agents and the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, and can expose any flow as a tool to external AI agents through its MCP server. It runs in the cloud, on-prem or air-gapped and is Apache 2.0 licensed.
pricing_detail: Open Source edition is free (Apache 2.0); Enterprise Edition and Kestra Cloud are annual subscriptions priced via sales, no public price (kestra.io/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026).

name: FloGPT
description: FloGPT is an AI chat and voice agent platform with a built-in AI CRM: embed a chat widget on your website, run AI phone agents around the clock, and handle chat, voice, email, SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook conversations from one inbox, all grounded in your own knowledge base.
pricing_detail: Freemium: free plan ($0/month plus usage for calls and SMS, 100 messages), then Starter $49/month, Growth $149/month or Professional $399/month, each plus usage for calls and SMS; prices as listed on its site

name: Reference to Video
description: Reference to Video turns product photos into 6-second AI ad clips for ecommerce and social: upload a product image, pick a shot style (showcase, lifestyle UGC, close-up detail or slow camera move) and an aspect ratio, and get a vertical, landscape or square video in 480p or 720p. Its reference mode treats the photo as a strict guide for tighter product fidelity and camera control.
pricing_detail: Paid: no free plan; one-time credit packs from $4.99 for 400 credits or $9.99 for 900 credits (valid 365 days), plus monthly and yearly plans; each 6-second clip costs 80-240 credits depending on mode and resolution; prices as listed on its site

name: Motion Transfer
description: Motion Transfer animates a character photo by copying the movement from a reference video: the photo sets the look while the clip drives gestures, expressions and body motion. Upload your own 4-30 second clip or pick a ready-made motion template, choose the model, resolution, length and aspect ratio in settings, see a credit estimate first, then preview and download the result. It also includes general AI image and video generation from one shared credit balance.
pricing_detail: Freemium: free Basic plan with one-time signup credits (the site banner advertises 60; the pricing page lists 18) and watermarked downloads; Starter $8.30/month billed yearly ($100/year, 2,400 credits), Pro $30/month billed yearly ($49.90 month-to-month), Business $49.90/month billed yearly; prices as listed on its site

name: Teebots
description: Teebots is a free desktop app that keeps a small team of AI bots on your own computer. Each bot can use a different model through your own API key, with requests going straight to the provider, and keeps its own private memory alongside a shared group memory. Put several bots in one group chat and @mention one to hand it a task, or let them pass steps to each other. Bots can work with files in their own folder, run commands, use skills including MCP and browse in their own browser, but they stop and wait for your approval before submitting or paying for anything. Scheduled daily or weekly jobs keep running from the menu bar. Chats, memory, files and logins stay local. Available for Mac (Apple silicon) now, with Windows and Linux coming soon.
pricing_detail: Free: the app costs nothing; model usage is billed to the API key you add. macOS (Apple silicon, v0.1.2) now; Windows and Linux coming soon

name: HaveTML
description: HaveTML lets AI agents publish what they make as a permanent share link. Ask Claude, Cursor or any MCP client to publish HTML, Markdown, JSON or YAML, and you get a sandboxed link anyone can open without logging in. Each link keeps its version history, supports comments, and can be set to private, unlisted or public.
pricing_detail: Free $0; Pro $6/mo or $60/yr; Team $20/mo

name: PeekPanda
description: PeekPanda is competitor research for iOS apps. Open any app to see the Meta ads it keeps paying for and how long each has run, the US App Store searches it ranks for, and which of its posts went viral. Use it in the web app, or add its MCP server so Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor can answer questions about any iOS competitor.
pricing_detail: Peek $59/mo; Panda $99/mo; $1 three-day trial

name: HireDov
description: HireDov is an AI sourcing agent. Describe what you need to buy and its agent, Dov, finds qualified suppliers, sends each a tailored request for quote in their own language, chases every reply and brings the quotes back to one dashboard to compare; first quotes usually arrive within a few days. You see the suppliers it finds before you pay.
pricing_detail: Pro $299/mo (100 credits); Business $799/mo (400 credits)

name: System One API
description: System One API is the hosted decision API behind TypeSafe Jev, with an open-source TypeScript SDK for AI agents. Where the TypeSafe Jev listing covers the decision model itself, this listing covers the developer API and console: send text or app context and get back a typed choice, a score or a yes/no probability for routing tools, ranking results and checking conditions, with API keys, call logs and credit use managed in one place.
pricing_detail: 100 free credits on sign-up; Starter $10 for 10,000 prepaid credits; no subscription

name: Financial Cents MCP
description: The Financial Cents MCP server connects an accounting, bookkeeping or tax firm's Financial Cents practice-management account to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor and other MCP clients. Staff can ask about overdue work, unpaid invoices or missing client tax documents in plain English and have the assistant log time or create tasks, with each connection bound to one firm, your own permissions applied, writes confirmed in the client and deletes not offered at all. It is a hosted server signed in with OAuth and comes with the Scale plan.

name: Userpilot Agent Analytics
description: Userpilot Agent Analytics shows product teams how users actually get on with the AI agent inside their app. It reads the agent's conversations at scale and reports whether people got what they needed or left frustrated, so teams can see where the agent fails, which requests it can't handle and how agent use ties back to product engagement, alongside Userpilot's existing product analytics.

name: Tulimoa Memory
description: Tulimoa Memory is a hosted, shared memory store for AI agents and agent swarms. Agents write what they learn into it during the day; overnight a separate model sorts those notes into a knowledge graph with associative recall, and each agent starts the morning with a short briefing so it reads less and knows more. It is billed per call, with starting credit to try it.

name: Keboola MCP Server
description: Keboola's official MCP server lets AI assistants and coding agents work with a Keboola data project: browse storage tables and buckets, read and write SQL transformations, run and debug jobs and components, and build data flows from a chat. It can run locally or as Keboola's hosted remote server, with access scoped to the project token or OAuth sign-in you grant.

name: Speakeasy Gram
description: Gram is Speakeasy's open-source platform for building, hosting and governing MCP servers. Teams can turn APIs into curated MCP toolsets, host them, and manage which agents and people may use which servers from one control plane, with sign-in, access policies and usage visibility; its own MCP server lets an agent manage that setup directly.

name: SuprSend MCP
description: SuprSend's official hosted MCP server gives AI agents and coding assistants access to a SuprSend notification workspace. An agent can look up and manage users and lists, inspect and edit notification workflows and templates, and read delivery data across email, SMS, push, Slack and in-app inbox channels without leaving the chat or editor.
